questions.question: A person sold two items selling each for ₹42,600. On the first item, he made a loss of 25%, while on the second, he gained 20%. Find his overall percentage gain or loss, giving your answer correct to one place of decimal.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A person sold two items selling each for ₹42,600. On the first item, he made a loss of 25%, while on the second, he gained 20%. 

**Calculation:**

By selling at Rs 42600 he loses by 25 % 

So cost price will be 42600 × 4/3 = Rs 56800

Again By selling at Rs 42600 he makes a profit by 20 % 

So the cost price will be 42600 × 5/6 = Rs 35500

Total cost price will be 56800 + 35500 = 92300

Total sp will be 42600 × 2 = Rs 85200

Loss amount is 92300 - 85200 = 7100 

Loss percentage will be (7100/92300) × 100 = 7.69 % ≈ 7.7 %

**∴ The correct option is** 2

questions.question: A man invested ₹4,500 at 5% per annum and ₹5,500 at 8% per annum simple interest. Both investments were for 4 years each. The amount received from the lower rate of interest is what per cent (rounded off to the nearest integer) of the amount received from the higher rate of interest?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Interest % for 4 years: **Lower rate** = 5% × 4 = 20% | **Higher rate** = 8% × 4 = 32%.

Amount 1 (Lower) = 4500 × 120% = 5400.

Amount 2 (Higher) = 5500 × 132% = 7260.

Required % = (5400 ÷ 7260) × 100 ≈ 74%.

**∴ The correct answer is 74%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Case 1: **Principal (P₁)** = ₹4,500, **Rate (R₁)** = 5%, **Time (T)** = 4 years.

Case 2: **Principal (P₂)** = ₹5,500, **Rate (R₂)** = 8%, **Time (T)** = 4 years.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = P + SI

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/014eb89a152d14c5db95494ee58c0713a939a82738e4545deeebd6c6269dbb30.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI₁ = (4500 × 5 × 4) ÷ 100 = 900

⇒ Amount₁ (lower rate) = 4500 + 900 = ₹5,400

⇒ SI₂ = (5500 × 8 × 4) ÷ 100 = 1760

⇒ Amount₂ (higher rate) = 5500 + 1760 = ₹7,260

⇒ Required Percentage = (5400 ÷ 7260) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = 54000 ÷ 726 ≈ 74.38%

⇒ Rounded off to the nearest integer = 74%

**∴ The correct answer is 74%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Concept

Interest is calculated only on the initial **Principal** amount for every year. SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Amount in Simple Interest

The total **Amount** (A) received at the end of the period is the sum of Principal and Interest: A = P(1 + RT/100).

Effective Rate of Interest

The total interest earned can be expressed as a single **effective percentage** of the principal, which is (Rate × Time)%.

questions.question: If the difference between the simple interest and the compound interest for 3 years at the rate of 10% per annum on a certain sum is equal to ₹310, then that sum of money is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For **3 years**, the difference between **CI** and **SI** is: D = P × (R/100)² × (3 + R/100)

⇒ 310 = P × (10/100)² × (3 + 10/100)

⇒ 310 = P × (1/100) × (31/10)

⇒ 310 = P × (31/1000)

⇒ **Principal (P)** = (310 × 1000) ÷ 31 = 10,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10,000.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Rate (R)** = 10% = 1/10, **Time (T)** = 3 years, **Difference (CI − SI)** = ₹310.

**Formula Used:** **Unitary Method** where **Principal** = (Denominator)Time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5aa57e29d6ac878be1022e8328217f0cc5f754a8788d650a44bdc9aac4bbddbe.png] 

⇒ Let **Principal** = 10³ = 1000 units.

⇒ **Simple Interest (SI)** for 3 years = 100 + 100 + 100 = 300 units.

⇒ **Compound Interest (CI)** for 3 years = 300 (SI) + 10 + 20 + 1 = 331 units.

⇒ **Difference** = 331 − 300 = 31 units.

⇒ 31 units = ₹310

⇒ 1 unit = ₹10

⇒ **Principal** = 1000 units × ₹10 = ₹10,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10,000.**

**__Additional Information__**

Difference for 2 Years

The difference between **CI** and **SI** for 2 years is calculated using the formula: Difference = P × (R/100)².

Effective Rate of Interest

For a **Rate** of 10%, the effective **Compound Interest** rate for 3 years is 33.1%, while the **Simple Interest** rate is 30%.

Compound Interest Amount Formula

The total amount after **n years** is given by: A = P × (1 + R/100)ⁿ.
